# Difference of Squares — Factor a Difference Instantly

## The identity to remember

$$
a^2-b^2=(a+b)(a-b)
$$

**Every symbol explained:** a and b are any numbers; the superscript 2 means multiplying the number by itself; parentheses are two factors whose product reproduces the difference.

**Substitute actual numbers:** Choose a=13, b=7. Instead of 169−49, calculate (13+7)(13−7)=20×6=120. Check 169−49=120.

## Why it is true

Expand (a+b)(a−b)=a²−ab+ab−b²; the mixed terms cancel. Geometrically, the area left after removing a b-by-b square from an a-by-a square can be rearranged into a rectangle with sides a+b and a−b when a≥b≥0.

## When to recognise it

When you see a perfect square minus a perfect square, factor before doing arithmetic. In integer algorithms, test a²−b²=N by finding factor pairs x=a−b and y=a+b with equal parity.

## Algorithm or number puzzle application

For N=45, select factor pair 5×9. Then a=(5+9)/2=7 and b=(9−5)/2=2. Indeed 7²−2²=49−4=45.

## Assumptions and pitfalls

Integer factor-pair reconstruction requires x and y to share parity. Squaring with fixed-width integers can overflow; algebraic equivalence does not prevent machine overflow.

## Your turn

Write x²−16 as a product, then evaluate 1001²−999² without squaring either number.

**Memory rule:** Understand the cancellation or construction that produces the identity. Re-derive the rule from two small numbers, then say aloud when you would use it.
